points.description: States that a higher priority process/task is blocked, delayed or prevented from running (not getting the CPU).
points.partial_credit: Half or full if only vaguely says priorities get mixed up or a high priority process waits, without a cause.

points.description: Says the cause is a lower priority process holding a resource (lock/shared resource) that the higher priority process needs, so the lower one effectively runs first.
points.partial_credit: Half if mentions a lower priority process interfering or running ahead without the resource link.

rubric.notes: Full marks for a one-line definition saying a higher priority process is kept waiting/not getting the CPU because a lower priority process holds a needed resource, in any wording. Give 1 mark if only one of the two ideas is present or the answer is vague (e.g., low priority runs before high priority). Give 0 for unrelated or wrong definitions; extra remarks do not cost marks.
